scope: Common SwiftUI settings menu, appearance picker and avatar rendering/URL policy on existing native and legacy hosts. Retain preference archives, diagnostics and logout warning; retire one-use appearance wrapper and unused app digest extensions. No grading, writer, sync, schema, API transport or credential migration change.

productionSwift.scope: Physical lines in app-owned tracked/new App/**/*.swift and Shared/Sources/**/*.swift; excludes Pods, Tests, AppTests, AppStoreScreenshots, FontScreenshotter and the two owner-only annotated files. Includes all changed production files, not merely deleted/moved ones. Test, resource and documentation lines are reported separately, not hidden as production Swift.

lineCountMeaning: This supplies native appearance/avatar and a common settings surface; it adds 81 net production lines, rather than claiming a cleanup reduction. The old wrapper and hash helpers are removed after their replacements are wired.

testCoverage.shared: Three parameterized avatar functions cover official normalization/hash, empty-address fallback and the exact legacy URL/cache contract at 80, 160 and 240 pixels. They replace the app-only SDK digest test; all other shared/hosted behavior remains.
testCoverage.hosted: The disconnected-settings regression follows the consolidated account state and also requires an empty avatar. An initial compile failure exposed old field references; the final assertions are ported, not disabled.
testCoverage.phoneAndTablet: Four existing cases per device cover menu/lesson order and persistence, review dependencies/download routes, isolated notifications, appearance/email/subject settings and cancellation of logout. All exercise/account data is synthetic.

nativeMacAutomation.reason: The runner timed out enabling UI automation before app launch. No selected native cases ran; this is not a passing gate or a diagnosed product defect.

nativeMacDirect.kind: Direct app-window CUA observations in this chat; not XCUITest
nativeMacDirect.configuration: Debug --review-fixture -ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES, isolated in-memory service/store and fixture defaults/notification client.
observed: Synthetic review fixture / Level 1 remained visible; no review was started or answered.
Settings exposed the same four pages, version, Saved work and WaniKani account actions.
Dark, fixture@example.invalid and Notify for all available reviews = on persisted after closing/reopening settings in the first direct run.
In the final direct run, selecting Light changed the sheet to its light rendering; email/reminder values remained present.
After returning Home and opening Reviews, reviewSettings.appearance showed Light, proving the same appearance owner.
Done returned to Home; the fixture app was then closed. Screenshots were limited to its own sheet/window.
nativeMacDirect.limits: These observations do not prove all three automated Mac cases, restart persistence, active-window accent color, physical delivery or a signed upgrade. The fixture resets its defaults at launch. The final Mac debug UI sources match the observed build; later iOS-only wrapper/project-reference retirement does not alter those Mac components.

preferences: Native appearance merges into existing StoredReviewPreferences; a string AppStorage value holds the custom avatar address in injected defaults. Legacy enum/email archives and the archived fallback address remain. Avatar fetches are deferred during native Settings editing; URL normalization omits the plain address.
nativeBoundaries: The menu and appearance controls are SwiftUI. Version selection uses the native text-selection API. Temporary iOS lifecycle/navigation/window-style callbacks and its archived preference stores still bridge the legacy coordinator; no new UIKit/AppKit UI adapter is added.

initialIntegrationFailure.resolution: Port old navigation username/level references to navigation.account and retain the same cleared-state assertions plus avatar nil. Final hosted suite passes 92.

remaining: Native review ordering, batch caps and leech thresholds; diagnostics/account-action parity; preference archive/fallback-avatar handoff.
Production native iOS scene/bootstrap/writer/background ownership and signed-device parity.
Mac automated launch/reopen and active-window visual acceptance; physical speech, IME, notification/watch/media acceptance and other tracked goal gates.
limits: No real WaniKani exercises, OS permission/security changes, hosted Actions pass, new dependency/tool publication, PR or push. iOS Release retains legacy framework/protobuf warnings; diagnostics are incremental rather than a whole-project warning audit.
rootAndMainboard: No parent manifest, Mainboard implementation or unrelated owner changes were edited/staged.
